aquinas-five-ways.label: Can we even know the truth?
aquinas-five-ways.prompt: Can the mind reach truth at all, before we test any argument?

aquinas-five-ways.label: Objections to God
aquinas-five-ways.prompt: What are the strongest objections to the existence of God, and how do we respond?

aquinas-five-ways.label: What is God like?
aquinas-five-ways.prompt: If the arguments succeed, what must this first being actually be?

can-we-know-truth.label: Can reason show that God exists?
can-we-know-truth.prompt: Before revelation, we can ask what unaided reason discovers.

objections-to-god.label: What is God like?
objections-to-god.prompt: If the arguments succeed, what must this first being actually be?

why-god.label: Can we even know the truth?
why-god.prompt: Before any argument for God, we ask whether truth exists and whether the mind can reach it.

why-god.label: Can reason show that God exists?
why-god.prompt: Before revelation, we can ask what unaided reason discovers.

transition.label: Which God?
transition.prompt: Reason has brought us to the God of classical theism. The next road asks which God this is — whether He is personal, and whether He has spoken.

which-god-can-reveal.label: What about other faiths?
which-god-can-reveal.prompt: Before naming the one who speaks, how does this God relate to Islam, deism, and Eastern conceptions?

which-god-can-reveal.label: What are the objections to this God?
which-god-can-reveal.prompt: A personal, self-revealing God of Israel draws hard objections — meet the strongest ones before going further.

which-god-can-reveal.label: Why the God of Israel?
which-god-can-reveal.prompt: Of all the claimants to revelation, why the covenant God of Abraham?

which-god-monotheism.label: Is the first cause personal?
which-god-monotheism.prompt: If there is one ultimate source, the next question is whether it has mind and will, or is a blind principle.

which-god-objections.label: What about other faiths?
which-god-objections.prompt: How does the God reason reaches relate to Islam, deism, and the Eastern conceptions?

which-god-objections.label: Why the God of Israel?
which-god-objections.prompt: With the hardest objections in view, the path still narrows to one covenant God — why the God of Abraham?

which-god-other-faiths.label: But what about the objections?
which-god-other-faiths.prompt: Comparing traditions raises sharp challenges — isn't choosing one arrogant, and is this God even good?

which-god-other-faiths.label: Why the God of Israel?
which-god-other-faiths.prompt: Having weighed the claimants, why the covenant God of Abraham in particular?

which-god-personal.label: Could God speak to us?
which-god-personal.prompt: If this God is personal, could He reveal Himself — and how would we recognize it?

which-god.label: Why one God, not many?
which-god.prompt: Reason's own arguments reach a single unlimited being — begin by seeing why the ultimate source must be one.

transition.label: Why Jesus?
transition.prompt: If the God of Israel is the one who speaks, the next question is whether He entered history — whether He became man in Jesus of Nazareth.

jesus-divine-claims.label: But doesn't that break monotheism?
jesus-divine-claims.prompt: If Jesus is God alongside the Father, how is that not two gods, after reason proved God is one?

jesus-divine-claims.label: Did Jesus fulfill prophecy?
jesus-divine-claims.prompt: Before the Resurrection, do the Hebrew Scriptures' messianic expectations converge on Jesus?

jesus-divine-claims.label: The Resurrection
jesus-divine-claims.prompt: If Jesus claimed a divine authority, the next question is whether He vindicated it by rising from the dead.

jesus-gospel-reliability.label: Did Jesus claim to be God?
jesus-gospel-reliability.prompt: If the Gospels are reliable historical sources, the first question they raise is who Jesus claimed to be.

jesus-objections.label: Did Jesus found a Church?
jesus-objections.prompt: If the claim withstands its hardest objections, the next question is whether the risen Christ founded a visible Church.

jesus-ot-prophecy.label: If Jesus is God, are there two gods?
jesus-ot-prophecy.prompt: How can Jesus be divine without breaking the one God reason reached?

jesus-ot-prophecy.label: The Resurrection
jesus-ot-prophecy.prompt: Prophecy points to who the Messiah would be; the Resurrection asks whether Jesus vindicated the claim.

jesus-resurrection.label: Objections to Jesus
jesus-resurrection.prompt: Sit with the hardest objections: the legend theory, natural explanations of the Resurrection, and the Gospels themselves.

jesus-resurrection.label: Did Jesus found a Church?
jesus-resurrection.prompt: If the Resurrection vindicates His authority, the next question is whether He established a visible Church to carry it on.

jesus-trinity.label: Did Jesus fulfill prophecy?
jesus-trinity.prompt: With the monotheism worry answered — do the Hebrew Scriptures' messianic expectations converge on Jesus?

jesus-trinity.label: The Resurrection
jesus-trinity.prompt: Or go straight to the decisive question — did Jesus vindicate the claim by rising from the dead?

jesus-who-was-he.label: Can we trust the Gospels?
jesus-who-was-he.prompt: The claim rests on history, so the first question is whether the Gospels are sources we can reason from.

why-jesus.label: Who was Jesus?
why-jesus.prompt: Before weighing the evidence, be clear about the man of history and the claim Christianity makes about him.

transition.label: Why the Church?
transition.prompt: If the risen Christ founded a visible Church and gave it authority to teach, the next question is where that Church is to be found today.

church-authority.label: Objections to the Church
church-authority.prompt: Before drawing things together, it is fair to test the claim against its hardest objections.

church-authority.label: Where the path has led
church-authority.prompt: With the Catholic claim set out in full, the path draws together toward a decision.

church-founded-by-christ.label: Which Church is it?
church-founded-by-christ.prompt: If Christ founded a Church meant to endure, the next question is how to recognize it among the many that claim His name.

church-four-marks.label: Scripture, Tradition, and authority
church-four-marks.prompt: If this is the Church Christ founded, the next question is how His revelation is preserved and who has authority to interpret it.

church-objections.label: Where the path has led
church-objections.prompt: With the objections met, the path draws together toward a decision.

church-recognizing-it.label: The four marks
church-recognizing-it.prompt: Historical continuity shows where to look; the creed's four marks show what to look for.

why-the-church.label: Did Christ found a Church?
why-the-church.prompt: Did Christ establish a visible Church and give it a teaching office?

transition.label: Coming Home
transition.prompt: If the path has led here, the question is no longer whether the Church is true but what to do about it — how to come home.

coming-home.label: I'm not yet Christian
coming-home.prompt: The case is persuasive, but you have not yet believed or been baptized.

coming-home.label: I'm Christian but not Catholic
coming-home.prompt: You love Christ in another tradition and have come to see the Catholic claim.

coming-home.label: I was Catholic and drifted away
coming-home.prompt: You were baptized Catholic and have been away — and you are being waited for.

home-not-yet-catholic.label: What the Church offers
home-not-yet-catholic.prompt: What full communion actually adds — above all, the Eucharist and the sacraments.

home-not-yet-catholic.label: What holds people back
home-not-yet-catholic.prompt: The particular hesitations that come with leaving a tradition you have loved.

home-not-yet-catholic.label: How to begin
home-not-yet-catholic.prompt: The concrete path into full communion for the already-baptized.

home-not-yet-christian.label: Why believe and practice?
home-not-yet-christian.prompt: Belief is not the finish line — it asks to be lived. Here is why that step is worth taking.

home-not-yet-christian.label: How to begin
home-not-yet-christian.prompt: The concrete first step for someone entering the Church from outside.

home-not-yet-christian.label: What the Church offers
home-not-yet-christian.prompt: Before deciding, it is worth seeing what is actually being held out to you.

home-obstacles.label: How to begin
home-obstacles.prompt: When the obstacle loses its grip, here is the first concrete step.

home-obstacles.label: What the Church offers
home-obstacles.prompt: The obstacles are only half the picture — weigh them against what is actually held out to you.

home-returning-catholic.label: What holds people back
home-returning-catholic.prompt: If something specific is keeping you away, it is worth naming it and meeting it honestly.

home-returning-catholic.label: How to begin again
home-returning-catholic.prompt: When you are ready, the way back is simpler and gentler than you may fear.

home-what-church-offers.label: What holds people back
home-what-church-offers.prompt: If this is what is offered, what keeps people from it — and how each hesitation is met.

home-what-church-offers.label: How to begin
home-what-church-offers.prompt: The practical first step toward receiving what is described here.

home-why-practice.label: How to begin
home-why-practice.prompt: If belief is meant to be lived, here is where the living starts.

transition.label: Begin Living the Faith
transition.prompt: You have come home. Now the faith becomes something you live — prayed, practised, and deepened day by day. Step into Discover Catholicism.
